checks.title: A deployer issues a generated password and a person's mail app logs in with it
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: A generated password from the platform secret logs a mail app in
  Given a deployer has generated a password for user "ana" with @rafters/mail-auth-basic
  And the deployer has added its entry to the login list in the platform secret
  When ana's mail app logs in over IMAP with that password, selects INBOX and fetches a message
  Then the login succeeds and the message is returned
  When the same mail app logs in as "ana" with a different password
  And it logs in as "nobody", a user not on the list, with ana's password
  Then both logins are refused with NO and the connection stays usable for another attempt
proves: SHALL offer a prebuilt login, @rafters/mail-auth-basic, that checks a password against a list in a platform secret
SHALL ... with passwords that are generated and never chosen (the issuing path a deployer uses)
intent direction.proposals[3]: a work inbox feels like the mailbox people already use (read from their own mail app)
toy 01a1a4c4: imaplib logged in, selected and fetched through the real session with a list from a binding
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: A deployer and a mail app meet it through IMAP over several calls (generate, configure, login, select, fetch), so it is a whole behaviour, not one rule.

checks.title: A mail app that reconnects often keeps logging in while wrong guesses from one address stop at 10 in 5 minutes
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: Reconnects are not refused, guesses stay at the limit
  Given ana's mail app connects from address A with her correct generated password
  When it logs in 30 times within 5 minutes
  Then every one of those logins succeeds
  When, still inside that window, address A sends wrong passwords interleaved with further correct logins
  Then the first 10 wrong passwords are answered NO for a wrong password
  And every later attempt from address A in the window is refused, the correct password included, without being checked
  And a mail app on address B logs in with its correct password
  When 5 minutes pass with no attempts from address A
  Then ana's mail app on address A logs in again
proves: SHALL ... a limit of 10 attempts per client address in a 5-minute window around any strategy
SHALL ... from which a correct password gets its slot back, so a mail app that reconnects often is not refused and wrong guesses stay at the limit
toy 01a1a4c4: without refund a correct password is refused after 10 attempts in 5 minutes (seen failure); 'refund only lets extra correct passwords through' was left unverified
toy 01a1ae1d: the test controls the window's clock instead of waiting 5 minutes
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The limit and the refund are met by a mail app and a guesser over many connections through IMAP, and the refund failure only shows across a sequence of attempts.

checks.title: A strategy author runs the contract suite in workerd and it passes good strategies and fails broken ones
checks.gherkin:
Scenario: The contract suite tells a sound strategy from a broken one
  Given the contract suite running in workerd
  When a strategy author runs it against the basic strategy, alone and wrapped in the limiter
  Then every clause passes both times
  When the author runs it against a strategy whose own work counter shows less work for an unknown user than for a wrong password
  Then the suite fails, naming the clause that an unknown user and a wrong password do the same work
  When the author runs it against a strategy that fails instead of refusing a user name of 502 bytes or more
  Then the suite fails, naming the clause that an oversized user is refused like any unknown user
proves: SHALL offer a contract suite any strategy can run in workerd, whose work rule is that an unknown user and a wrong password do the same work, by a counter the strategy supplies
SHALL ... costing one hash per attempt whether or not the user exists (basic passes the work clause)
SHALL ... limit ... around any strategy (the suite passes wrapped as well as plain)

toy 01a1a4c4: 15 of 15 on basic, plain and wrapped, in workerd; 516-753 percent gap with no dummy; a user of 502 bytes or more made a KV get throw and closed the session with EOF (seen failure), and the port needs 'a contract clause'
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The suite is itself the deliverable a strategy author uses, and proving it catches what it must takes several runs against several strategies through its surface.

checks.title: Basic checks a golden table of entries with one PBKDF2-SHA256 hash at 100,000 iterations over the client's octets
checks.rule: For every row of the golden table (correct password, wrong password, unknown user, a password with octets 0x80-0xFF as the client sends them, and an entry whose iterations are not 100,000), basic returns the expected mailbox or null and its work counter shows exactly one PBKDF2-SHA256 hash at 100,000 iterations over the client's octets; the entry not at 100,000 never logs in.
proves: SHALL ... PBKDF2-SHA256 at 100,000 iterations over the client's octets, costing one hash per attempt whether or not the user exists
toy 01a1a4c4 must_hold: hash the client's octets; generators hash UTF-8; octets() truncates above 0xFF
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Each row is one call to the strategy, and the contract suite asserts only equal work, so an exact count, the iteration figure and the octet encoding can fail without any scenario failing.

checks.title: Concurrent attempts from one address admit exactly 10, and refused ones do no hash
checks.rule: When 50 attempts from one address race the limiter's take, exactly 10 reach the strategy and the refused 40 cause no hash, because take is one synchronous transaction.
proves: SHALL ... a limit of 10 attempts per client address in a 5-minute window
toy 01a1a4c4: take as one synchronous transaction held 15 races of 50 at exactly 10, refusals hashed 0
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: The behaviour scenario sends attempts one after another and never enters a race, and a guesser cannot see through IMAP how many hashes a refusal cost.

checks.title: The limiter's count survives eviction of whatever holds it
checks.rule: Attempts counted for an address before the object holding the count is evicted with hibernation still count after it, so an 11th attempt in the window is refused.
proves: SHALL ... a limit of 10 attempts per client address in a 5-minute window
reflection 01a1a48e: everything runs at the edge with no in-memory counters
toy 01a1ae1d: evict(stub, { webSockets: 'hibernate' }) reproduces the runtime's eviction; ctx.abort() is not eviction
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: Eviction is not something a guesser or mail app can cause or see through IMAP, and the behaviour scenario never evicts.

checks.title: No credential reaches stored state
checks.rule: After a run of correct, wrong and unknown-user logins through the real session, a byte scan of every state file and the D1 database finds none of the passwords, their hashes or their salts.
proves: SHALL: No credential SHALL reach stored state
toy 01a1a4c4: no credential in D1 or any of 4,786 state files, by byte scan
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: It is a never-property, and no user can see stored state through a public surface.

checks.title: The generator never takes a chosen password
checks.rule: The package's generator accepts no password as input and each call returns a fresh random password with its entry, so the only passwords the list can hold are generated ones.
proves: SHALL ... with passwords that are generated and never chosen
reflection 01a1a48e: the hash cannot protect a weak password, so passwords are generated and long, never chosen
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: It is a never-property of one function; the login scenario shows a generated password works but cannot show a chosen one is impossible.

checks.title: The package is MIT and imports nothing from the service layer
checks.rule: The package manifest declares MIT, and its resolved import graph contains no module from mail's service layer.
proves: SHALL: the package SHALL be MIT and import nothing from the service layer
reflection 01a1a48e: prebuilt strategies in separate MIT packages so core ships no credential store
checks.why_not_the_other_kind: No user meets the licence or import graph through a public surface, and it is one static fact.

failure_ways.way: The platform secret is missing or malformed, so reading the list throws
failure_ways.caught_by: No SHALL settles what the client sees; reported under gaps

failure_ways.way: A strategy's store hangs, holding the login and its limiter slot
failure_ways.caught_by: No SHALL settles a timeout; reported under gaps

failure_ways.way: Store time differs between an unknown user and a wrong password even with the dummy hash (about 0.1 ms on local KV)
failure_ways.caught_by: No SHALL breaks: the work rule is defined by the strategy's counter, not by wall time

failure_ways.way: The login list outgrows the platform secret's size (about 27 entries in a 5 KB variable)
failure_ways.caught_by: No SHALL in this requirement sets a list size; no SHALL breaks

failure_ways.way: A limiter refusal reads as NO and counts toward the session's 3-strike BYE
failure_ways.caught_by: No SHALL breaks: the refusal still refuses, and the reconnecting mail app is protected by the refund

gaps.failure_way: The limit counts attempts in a fixed 5-minute window, so up to 20 attempts can land in 5 minutes across a boundary
gaps.question: Is the 5-minute window fixed or sliding? Both read as 'a 5-minute window', and the answer changes how the limiter stores its count.

gaps.failure_way: A strategy's store or the platform secret throws, or hangs
gaps.question: What must the contract require when a strategy's store fails: a NO with the attempt counted, a closed connection, or something else, and is there a deadline after which a hung store is treated as failed?

gaps.failure_way: A generated password is too short to survive offline guessing at 100,000 iterations
gaps.question: What minimum length or entropy must a generated password have?
